thread:
cheng: Quick sync — we need a decision on per-card max_tokens_per_batch and fallback behavior. Profiling surfaced a clear perf regression on L4 when we push token budgets up; also seeing kernel selection flip to a slow matmul path when KV frag increases. Need a concise plan: soft vs hard caps, queue policy tweaks, and canary rollout params.

alex: TL;DR numbers from the latest microbench (attached in dashboard): A100 ~40k tokens/batch w/ stable throughput, H100 ~48k, A10 ~28k, T4 ~22k, L4 starts regressing past ~18k. KV cache occupancy reduces headroom on L4 by ~20%. Raw traces: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/2026-03-17/9832

maria: Uploaded the flamegraphs + kernel selector logs. L4 flips from kernel_fit_fast -> matmul-ntb at ~18k and GPU SM utilization becomes spiky. Also saw increased L2 thrash when slices cross 512-token boundaries. Suggests both token budget and slicing shape matter.

sam: Proposal draft: implement per-GPU soft_token_cap + hard_token_cap. Soft cap is used for normal scheduling (allows burst) and is subject to token-bucket smoothing; hard cap is absolute reject/fallback to smaller model variant. Example config: 
```json
{
  "per_gpu_caps": {
    "A100": {"soft_tokens": "40000", "hard_tokens": "48000", "max_batch_size": "12"},
    "H100": {"soft_tokens": "46000", "hard_tokens": "52000", "max_batch_size": "14"},
    "A10": {"soft_tokens": "26000", "hard_tokens": "32000", "max_batch_size": "10"},
    "T4":  {"soft_tokens": "20000", "hard_tokens": "24000", "max_batch_size": "8"},
    "L4":  {"soft_tokens": "16000", "hard_tokens": "20000", "max_batch_size": "6"}
  },
  "kv_frag_threshold": 0.6,
  "kernel_selector": "prefer_hybrid_on_kv_frag"
}
```

lisa: +1 to soft/hard caps. Two extra tweaks: 1) kernel_selector should bias to kernel_fit_hybrid when KV_frag > 0.6 (avoids matmul-ntb thrash on L4). 2) Queue policy: introduce small-request priority (<=256 tokens) to reduce head-of-line blocking for short latency traffic. Also reduce L4 max_batch_size to 5 in the canary to be conservative.

infra-ci-bot: perf-harness run 2026-03-17T11:24:07Z finished. Results summary: A100 throughput delta +0.6% @ soft=40k, H100 +0.8% @ soft=46k, A10 stable @26k, T4 stable @20k, L4 throughput -7.2% @20k (latency p95 increase). Full report: https://ci.redwood/reports/9832

alex: Given the CI numbers, I recommend the following immediate defaults: set L4 soft=16k hard=20k, T4 soft=20k hard=24k, A10 soft=26k hard=32k, A100/H100 keep current higher caps but enable token-bucket smoothing window=30s to avoid large bursts. Also enable kernel_selector bias for KV_frag>0.6.

maria: For canary we should also log these extra metrics: kernel_choice, kv_frag_ratio, per-slice-alloc (to compute fragmentation), and batch_shape histogram. Add a regression alert if throughput drops >5% or p95 latency increases >15% vs baseline for 10m.

sam: Canary rollout plan: 1) deploy config to 5% of L4 pool + 2 machines each for T4/A10 canaries, 2) run synthetic mixed workload (short+long) for 30m, 3) collect metrics + traces, 4) auto-rollback on alert. I'll run the canary tomorrow 09:00 PT and post artifacts.

cheng: Sounds good. One more thought: implement a fast-path in the queue policy to split oversized batches at enqueue time if KV_frag > 0.7 and model has high KV footprint — avoids selecting matmul-ntb later. That could be a follow-up quick patch.

alex: How do we define KV_frag in the agent? We currently compute it as kv_active_tokens / kv_capacity. If kv_capacity changes by quantization/packing, the threshold needs to be relative. I propose kv_frag_threshold be percentile-based (e.g., 75th) over the last 5m to avoid noisy flips.

lisa: Agreed. We'll use the 75th pct over 5m. Also, I'll open the PR to change kernel_selector heuristics and lower L4 max_batch_size in canary: PR #789.

sam: Repro command for perf harness (for whoever runs local repro):
```bash
./perf_harness --model gptx-3b --gpu L4 --seq 8192 --qps 200 --tokens-per-batch 20000 --kv-trace --output ./artifacts/l4-20k
```

infra-ci-bot: scheduled regression watch for PR #789. Will run nightly comparative job for 72h and post summary.

cheng: Great — next steps: sam runs canary, lisa lands kernel_selector PR, alex and maria set alert windows and baselines. We'll reconvene after canary artifacts are up. Thanks all :thumbsup:
